limits.title: macOS and iOS on non-Apple computers
limits.body: Linkspan will not run macOS or iOS software on non-Apple hardware. Apple licenses those systems for Apple hardware. Linkspan does not include an emulator, disk image, translation layer, or installer for them, and it does not describe how to build one. A Mac or iOS file can stay in the library so you can see what it is.

limits.title: iOS packages
limits.body: Linkspan will not install an IPA or a device .app bundle, including on a Mac. It does not decrypt App Store packages, remove DRM, or re-sign apps. On a Mac it can open an iOS app that is already installed, and it can launch a Simulator build of an app you compiled with Xcode.

limits.title: No iOS app
limits.body: There is no iOS version of Linkspan. The hosts are Android, Windows, Linux, macOS, and OpenHarmony. iOS software is only a guest, and only where the other limits on this page allow it.

limits.title: Windows
limits.body: Wine is kept for Windows programs. It opens native host windows. It is not a Windows license, and it is not used for OpenHarmony. Linkspan does not ship a Windows image, product key, or activation workaround. A slim Wine runtime can be downloaded from its own repository. A full Windows virtual machine needs an image and a license you already have.

limits.title: Google Play
limits.body: Linkspan does not include Google Play, Play Services, or a Google sign-in. An Android program has to be an APK you already have, or a package already installed in your own Android runtime.

limits.title: Programs are not downloaded
limits.body: Linkspan does not download applications, Apple system images, Flatpak runtimes, or snaps. Slim guest runtimes for Android, Linux, OpenHarmony, and Wine are downloaded when you open the app, from their own repositories, after the client IP chooses GitHub or a China mirror. Those images are not inside the Linkspan program.

limits.title: OpenHarmony, not HarmonyOS
limits.body: Harmony guests are OpenHarmony packages (.hap and OpenHarmony .app bundles). Linkspan runs them on a real OpenHarmony system. It does not translate them into Android or Windows programs, and it does not ship a HarmonyOS commercial image, Huawei signing keys, or an unofficial port. Unsigned packages install only in developer mode through the official installer.

limits.title: OpenHarmony host
limits.body: The OpenHarmony client runs OpenHarmony software on that device. It does not bundle guest images. Other guest systems are refused there. There is still no iOS host.

limits.title: Your programs and the engines
limits.body: You are responsible for the rights to the programs you run. Wine, Proton, QEMU, Lima, Waydroid, WSL, OpenHarmony, GTK, and the system package tools stay under their own licenses. Linkspan's own source is Apache-2.0 only.
